scoutLeads.why: `for owner, nss := range nsByOwner` iterates a Go map and populates `collided[ns]=owner` inside the loop; the surfaced conflict `Owner` field consumed by R26's auditor could be nondeterministic across process runs if a namespace could collide via more than one path.

`for ns, owners := range ownersByNS` iterates a map and appends `BindingConflict` entries to `ev.conflicts` in map order, so `Evaluation.Conflicts()` returns conflicts in a non-deterministic order across process runs, which any caller or test asserting on conflict order/index would flake on.

The `isInterior` exemption (`if _, isInterior := interior[owner]; isInterior { continue }`) is documented above as safe because 'nothing ever classes Owned against a pool' and 'pools are admin-written at both ends', but the repo's own DECISIONS-NEEDED.md P5 entry and the archived 2026-07-24 review record that an owner which is simultaneously a leaf (directly bound in >=2 namespaces) and named as an interior parent evades ConflictLeafOwnerSpansNamespaces entirely, letting a Run in one tenant's namespace mint a non-recallable Owned charge against another tenant.

The lendingAllows empty-borrower guard comment asserts 'An empty borrower is never lendable' -- true only because every caller currently derives borrower via ev.OwnerOf(run.Namespace); if a future caller passes a raw/unresolved owner string to lendingAllows the guarantee is enforced only by comment and calling convention, not the type system.

The rewritten comment states namespace equality is 'forge-proof' and 'strictly stronger' than the old owner-string check, an indicative claim about all future callers of promiseProvenanceValid; it is true only because Namespace is authenticated by the API server for real Segments, but nothing in the type system prevents a future caller from constructing a cover.Segment with an attacker-influenced Namespace field from an untrusted source.

ownerOf falls back to run.Namespace itself as the 'owner' key when in.Evaluation is nil, silently coarsening the funding-principal identity to the raw namespace string; if any caller path reaches reclaimUnfunded/runLottery without an Evaluation while the real evaluation would have derived the empty-owner fail-safe sentinel (conflicted/unbound namespace), the reclaim/lottery bucketing keys by the wrong identity.

confirmed.title: metrics.BudgetKey lacks a Namespace field, unlike funding.EnvelopeKey, causing cross-namespace gauge collisions

summaries.summary: Immortal-lease / cloned-obligation lens on r7pt2/tenancy-owner-from-namespace (HEAD 0b77fbe, 8 commits off e918ca6b), repo root /home/runner/work/jobtree/jobtree. Investigator read the playbook in full, enumerated every exit path of every function the diff adds or modifies (funding.deriveOwners/OwnerOf/Conflicts/lendingAllows/fill, resolver.ownerOf/reclaimUnfunded/runLottery, admission.Feasible, forecast.computeHeadroom/selectEnvelope, run_controller.Reconcile/reclaimForAdmission/activateReservation/opportunisticCoverPlan, plugin.promiseProvenanceValid, api/v1.validate). Rather than speculate, copied the tree to /tmp/probe/jobtree and to /tmp/mainref (git archive main) and ran seven executable probes through the pure engine. Headline result: the change did NOT leak a Lease -- probe 3 (checkpoint grace + conflicted namespace, 20 Reconciles over 20 simulated hours) closes every lease via failRun -> releaseRun, and probe 2 shows a Running run correctly coasts Unfunded with its lease open, the documented legal state. What the change DID leak is the sibling obligation: because ev.OwnerOf(run.Namespace) can now be "" and cover.Inventory.Plan turns an empty owner into FailureReasonInvalidRequest, activateReservation hits its "programmer error" early return and NEVER reaches failReservationNoEnvelope. Probe 6 on the branch vs the identical baseline on main proves a regression: delete a run's Budget after its reservation exists and main fails the reservation terminally on tick 1, while the branch loops "owner and flavor must be set" for 20 ticks with the reservation stuck Pending and its backlog gauge frozen forever. This falsifies R7-tenancy-amendment.md 4/14 C-2. Two further confirmed defects: Evaluation.Conflicts() has zero production consumers despite two doc-comments asserting R26 alarms on them, so an admin typo silently demotes a whole tenant's running work Owned->Unfunded (probe 2: 8 owned GPUs -> 8 unfunded), and probe 7 shows the very next competing admission closes it with ReclaimUnfunded -- a silent reaper with no event, no metric, no log; and promiseProvenanceValid's namespace-equality rewrite is NOT "strictly stronger" as its comment claims (probe 5: the sole committer accepts a Promise charge against a different owner's Budget in the same namespace, which the old owner-string check refused). The full unit suite is green on the branch -- nothing turns red for any of this.

This is a class-3 (last-writer-wins) adversarial review of branch r7pt2/tenancy-owner-from-namespace at commit 0b77fbe against main, covering an 8-commit, 82-file diff. The investigator read the adversarial-review playbook, copied the worktree to /tmp/jtscratch/repo to avoid writing into the repo, wrote and ran five throwaway probes, then deleted them and reran the suite clean. The overall verdict is that the change introduces no order dependence in any funding outcome: four metamorphic experiments (HandleNodeFailure over 120 lease/budget permutations x3 repeats, funding.Evaluate over 24 permutations x30 repeats, resolver.Resolve over 400 in-process repeats, and deriveOwners over 24 budget permutations) all returned byte-invariant results, and a negative control (breaking runPhaseTracker.apply's severity guard) correctly turned the existing rail red, confirming the experiments have teeth. However, two CONFIRMED, executed nondeterminisms were found in the new deriveOwners code, both confined to the diagnostic surface rather than the funding decision: collided[ns] = owner in pkg/funding/evaluate.go is a last-writer-wins scalar over a Go map (200 runs produced 2 distinct BindingConflict.Owner answers), and Conflicts() is appended in map order (200 runs produced 4 distinct orders) while the new test at tenancy_r7_test.go:53 already indexes conflicts[0] positionally. Their severity is capped because grep shows BindingConflict/Conflicts() has zero non-test consumers today, the doc comment claiming R26's ledger auditor consumes them is false as of this review, which the investigator argues is itself the reason to fix the shape now while the type is still free to change. The investigator also flags that the repo's class-3 permutation/repetition rail (controllers/order_independence_test.go) was not extended to cover the three new map iterations introduced in Evaluate, so both confirmed nondeterminisms shipped green. The full suite passed at go test ./... -count=3.

Investigator reviewed the 8-commit R7 pt2 stack (git diff main...HEAD @ 0b77fbe) through SIGNAL != REALITY (class 4), IDENTITY COARSENING (class 5) and GUARD BEFORE PREDICATE (class 6) lenses, after reading the adversarial-review-playbook and the binding sections of R7-tenancy-amendment.md and quota-semantics.md. Built a scratch Go module under /tmp importing pkg/funding, pkg/cover, pkg/resolver and ran four compiled reproductions. Key results: (1) the interior-tier exemption at evaluate.go:220 is a guard-before-predicate bug where the isInterior continue runs before the len(nss)>=2 match predicate, and the interior set is coarsened to 'any string in any Budget.Spec.Parents cluster-wide,' so one stray Parents entry lets a Run in an unrelated namespace take a non-borrowed 64-GPU Owned cover segment on a victim's envelope with conflicts==[] -- a cheaper trigger than the previously parked P5 record; (2) the fail-safe's documented 'coast' behavior is false: adding an unrelated-namespace Budget flips a live Owned lease to Unfunded, and resolver.Resolve with OnlyUnfunded:true (the exact call made on any tenant's admission with a deficit) then reclaims it, silently since Evaluation.Conflicts() has zero production consumers; (3) the empty-owner sentinel merges unbound/conflicted tenants into one lottery bucket, measured to skew a small tenant's share of reclaim cuts from 48% to 10% over 500 seeds; (4) promiseProvenanceValid dropped its seg.Owner check, letting Lease.Spec.Owner be set to any string by a forged Promise pod, confirmed by a new test asserting the absence of that check. Two questions (physical-liveness signals, and errors matched by text) came back clean with no findings.

Adversarial review of PR #127 (r7pt2/tenancy-owner-from-namespace, head 0b77fbe) across the half-plane/reapers lens. The investigator grepped the production diff for lease-closure and pod-deletion sites and found none introduced by this change; all newly reachable demotion doors (conflict/unbound namespace -> OwnerOf returning "", the lendingAllows empty-borrower guard) feed into three pre-existing, verified two-plane actors: applyResolution (run_controller.go:2157, 2181-2193), reclaimSquatter, and failRun/releaseRun (run_controller.go:2032). The checkpoint-grace exemption in applyResolution keys on run.Status.CheckpointDeadline, not a phase name (run_controller.go:2235). Using two compiled throwaway Go probes against commit 0b77fbe (built at /tmp/r7probe with a replace directive; no repo files were touched), the investigator reconfirmed the previously parked P5 finding: an owner leaf-bound in two namespaces plus named as a child budget's Parent produces zero conflicts and an Owned, non-demoting, cross-tenant charge (Finding 1, adjudicated as real and live on this HEAD). Probe B found map-order nondeterminism in Conflicts() ordering and surfaced Owner field (Finding 2, LOW, diagnostics-only). A latent, currently-unreachable-in-production identity-coarsening fallback in resolver.go was also identified (Finding 3, LOW). The investigator ruled that dropping the isInterior exemption is not a run-reaper under the design's ratified posture, but would create false alarms for legal multi-namespace pools. No pkg/invariant panics are added or strengthened in a way that trips on any legal state found; the invariants err too-weak (via the exemption) rather than reaper-direction. Quantified consequence: Finding 1 lets an attacker mint an unbounded-duration Owned charge (bounded only by victim envelope Concurrency, e.g. 4 of 8 GPUs in the probe) against a victim's budget, silently burning GPU-hours until exhaustion, at which point the victim's own legitimate work becomes reclaimable, with zero conflict/audit signal generated for R26's auditor to consume.

The investigator reviewed an 8-commit R7 pt2 stack (main...HEAD, head 0b77fbe) using playbook class 8 ('the test asserts the bug'), running mutation testing in a scratch copy at /tmp/r7mut/repo (no repo files were created/edited/deleted) plus direct reading of oracle/API-validation code. Ten mutations were run against the real suite. Seven core fail-safes were confirmed genuinely load-bearing (mutants went red): the empty-borrower guard in evaluate.go's lendingAllows, the leaf-owner-span fail-safe, the multi-owner fail-safe, OwnerOf's positive derivation path, and the namespace guards in promiseProvenanceValid. Three defenses were found NOT tested: (a) deleting the interior-tier exemption line in evaluate.go leaves the whole suite green because TestInteriorTierExemptFromInjectivity's pool owner is bound in only one namespace, and a concrete fixture was built reproducing a cross-tenant Owned-claim hazard with Conflicts() empty; (b) pkg/resolver.ownerOf survives both branches being replaced by a constant, and buildRun discards its namespace parameter via `_ = namespace`, structurally forbidding the fixture shape R7 newly makes reachable; (c) two test surfaces excluded from the default build were not updated — test/e2e/smoke_test.go's TestValidatingWebhookRejectsInvalidRun still provokes rejection via a now-legal stimulus (omitted spec.owner), and seven hack/e2e/*.sh scripts still kubectl-apply Run manifests carrying spec.owner. Additional findings: Evaluation.Conflicts() has zero production consumers despite documentation promising R26 alarms; two fixtures bind namespaces via envelope-less Budgets the API server rejects; and the change deleted the CRD 'empty owner' probe without adding a replacement regression test for the privilege escalation R7 exists to close. One inverted assertion was found in cmd/scheduler/plugin/gang_test.go, where an owner-consistency check was replaced with its opposite, contradicting R7-tenancy-amendment.md's stated rationale for keeping Lease.Spec.Owner as an audit-legible field.
